newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary bourse edges up in 1997's lowest turnover.
newsitem.headline: Hungary bourse edges up in 1997's lowest turnover.

text.p: A rangebound trading in Hungarian shares drove the BUX index a fraction higher in this year's lowest share turnover as investors were inactive before the U.S. Fed's meeting on Tuesday, traders and analysts said.
The BUX index closed at 5,093.27 points, up 8.47. BUX futures fell for all maturities by between 43.00 and 100.50 points. June BUX lost 43.00 points to end at 5,319.5 points.
Most of the market is certain that a rate rise will materialise and some traders believe that the market, paradoxically, will be able to benefit from higher rates.
"Expectations (of a rate rise) are already built in prices, and it's a possibility that shares will strengthen after a rise," said Tamas Revesz of Wintrust.
"But if the Fed leaves interest rates steady, uncertainty will remain and then the BUX may fall to 4,600 points."
Other analysts said a rate hike may have a selective negative impact on some Hungarian shares.

"If this (rate hike) results in a readjustment within American funds, this may have an impact on certain shares, even if the Hungarian capital market is not fundamentally linked to American interest rates," said Gabor Sitanyi, analyst at ING Barings in London.
Shares with a higher proportion of American investors, such as pharmaceuticals Richter, may be affected, he said.

Nevertheless, the Hungarian share market is the most sensitive among eastern European bourses to changes in U.S. interest rates, Sitanyi said, but added this sensitivity was far below that of Latin American emerging markets.
Many market players share the opinion that investors hold their cash waiting for new investment opportunities on the Budapest bourse.
Share offers in the near future include Richter and MOL, while the longer-term prospects include commercial vehicle maker Raba and electricity supplier Elmu Rt.

On Monday retailer Global outperformed the market by rising more than 11 percent or 200 forints to end at 2,000, after Tesco 's subsidiary Cheshunt Overseas Finance B.V., Global's majority owner, made a buyout offer for holders of Global shares at 2,100 forints or 7.48 pounds.

Textile producer Pannon-Flax dipped 20 forints to 900 forints. The company said earlier today it would propose the payout of a five percent dividend on its 1996 earnings after reinvesting its profits last year.
